title: Tiered Dedicated GPU Packages with Burst Credits and Autoscale Guardrails
creator: Priya Narang
description:
Goal: Define and validate a set of tiered Dedicated GPU packages that combine reserved capacity, a bounded burst credit pool, and autoscaling guardrails tied to SLA tiers. Outcome should be a clear offer that sales can sell to mid-market and enterprise customers, technical acceptance criteria for the infra team, and a runbook for entitlement enforcement and billing reconciliation.

Background: We currently sell Dedicated as a simple reserved capacity SKU with optional burst by exception. Sales asks for a predictable productized burst offering and simpler entitlement language in the contract/SQ. Engineering needs deterministic autoscale policies to avoid noisy neighbor incidents and cost overruns. This ticket coordinates product experiments with Pricing, Sales Eng, and Infra to converge on price points, credit sizing, and SLA definitions.

Scope: Pricing experiments (A/B) for 3 candidate packages (Standard, Premium, Enterprise), specification of burst credit behavior (recharge rate, capacity, preemption rules), autoscaling headroom and cooldown policies, and contract language drafts for security questionnaire implications (data isolation, audit logs, KMS). Not in scope: on-prem packaging and one-off legal negotiation for named customers (handled separately).
acceptance_criteria: Three candidate packages documented with expected throughput and GPU-hour pricing per tier
Burst credit mechanics fully specified (credit bucket size, recharge interval, max burst duration) and implementable by infra
Autoscale policy templates defined by GPU pool size, latency SLO thresholds, and cooldown windows
SLA matrix (uptime, latency P99 targets, scheduled maintenance windows) mapped to each tier
Pricing experiment plan with segmentation, sample sizes, and success criteria signed off by Sales and Finance
Draft contract language and SQ answers for dedicated offers created and reviewed by legal/security
Telemetry plan and dashboards defined to measure revenue impact, utilization, and SLO compliance
experiment_design: Hypotheses: A modestly higher per-GPU reserved price + small burst credit allocation increases ARR with minimal churn; customers value predictable burst behaviour over ad-hoc approvals.
Cohorts: 1) Existing dedicated customers offered upgrade path; 2) New customers during sign-up funnel; 3) High-throughput AI startups via AE outreach.

Variants: Variant A (Conservative) - small burst bucket (20% of reserve) + tight cooldown; Variant B (Balanced) - medium bucket (50%) + moderate cooldown; Variant C (Generous) - large bucket (100%) + long cooldown but higher price.
Duration & size: 8-week experiments per cohort with minimum of 30 customers or equivalent commitment tranche per variant to reach statistical confidence on conversion/upgrade metrics.
Billing & entitlements: Burst consumption consumed from pre-purchased credits; display in Console; automatic fallback to pay-as-you-go if credits exhausted (opt-in).
Rollout controls: Feature-flagged on Console / API; limit to regions US-EAST and EU-WEST for initial run; Sales enablement docs prepared before outbound offers.
metrics: Upgrade conversion rate (existing customers upgrading to Premium/Enterprise)
Net new ARR attributable to packaged offerings
Burst credit consumption rate (credits used / credits allocated)
SLO compliance (P95/P99 latency and error rate) during bursts
Incidents related to noisy neighbor or autoscale failures
Revenue per GPU-hour and realized gross margin vs baseline pricing
